name: @kolu/acp-harness
//exports: ONE door, and it is one on purpose: a second subpath would be a second way to reach a subprocess, and there is exactly one subprocess. What the door now hands out beside `startHarness` is the conversation layer itself — `Transcript`, `Turns`, the held list, and the `says`/`plus` rules over a change — because two products run one conversation each and both must be served by the same classes rather than by a copy in each.
//scripts: `test:daemon`, not `test:unit`: every test here but one spawns a real ACP agent as a detached process group (the fixture agents `@kolu/acp-client/testlib` hands out), which is the lane `just test-daemon` runs serially and `just test-unit` skips — the same reason `kolu-omp` declares it. A package declares ONE lane, so the pure `src/kolu.test.ts` rides along in it.
//dependencies: `@kolu/acp-client` RUNS THE PROTOCOL — this package holds one conversation on top of it and spawns nothing itself, so the SDK is the client's runtime dependency and no longer this one's (`packages/acp/src/manifest.test.ts` holds that). `effect` is a runtime dependency for the same reason: the client's verbs are Effects, and the one boundary in `conversation.ts` runs them. `kolu-common` is imported for the row and state TYPES alone — the harness writes that contract and never reaches for a daemon itself. `kolu-mcp` is reached ONLY at its `/fleetRef` leaf, which is the one definition of the `host/id` grammar a kolu call's args are written in; that subpath deliberately carries no MCP SDK and no padi-client, so the manifest above stays true. `@kolu/terminal-vocab` is reached ONLY at its `/terminalId` leaf, for `isTerminalId`: a string the agent wrote becomes a card's terminal only if it passes the same check the wire's row schema applies, so the reading and the encoder cannot disagree.
//devDependencies: Nothing but the toolchain: the fixture agents this suite spawns are `@kolu/acp-client`'s, and the client is a runtime dependency above.
